title: Derived-unit resolution calculation in a proper/open tower
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. Let $X,U,\overline X,Y,\overline Y,Z$ be Noetherian schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], where Noetherian means admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings. Suppose that $j:X\hookrightarrow U$, $b:U\hookrightarrow\overline X$, and $i:Y\hookrightarrow\overline Y$ are open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion], that $q:U\to Y$, $p:\overline X\to\overline Y$, and $s:\overline Y\to Z$ are proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], and that $pb=iq$. Put $a=bj$. On small etale sites use constant-$A$ module sheaves and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]; $Dk_!$ denotes exact termwise open extension and $Rt_*$ total derived direct image as in [def-amb-etale-compact-support]. Write $\chi:i_!q_*\xrightarrow{\sim}p_*b_!$ for the section-preserving proper-support identification [lem-cbc-proper-support-sheaf-composition], and $\Gamma_Q:Di_!Rq_*\to Rp_*Db_!$ for the specified proper/open comparison [lem-amb-unbounded-proper-open-interchange].

For any K-injective complex $J$ on $X$ [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions], choose K-injective resolutions $u:j_!J\to I$ on $U$, $v:b_!I\to M$ on $\overline X$, and $w:i_!q_*I\to L$ on $\overline Y$. Then $q_*I$ and $p_*M$ are K-injective, and there is a chain map $\ell:L\to p_*M$, unique up to homotopy subject to
$$\ell w\simeq (p_*v)\chi_I.$$
The following two maps, with source $s_*i_!q_*j_!J$ and target $s_*p_*M$, are chain homotopic:
$$ (s_*\ell)(s_*w)(s_*i_!q_*u)
\quad\text{and}\quad
(s_*p_*(v\circ b_!u))\,(s_*\chi_{j_!J}). $$
Moreover $v\circ b_!u:a_!J=b_!j_!J\to M$ is a K-injective resolution. With the canonical open-extension and derived-direct-image composition identifications [lem-cbc-extension-zero-composition, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition], the first path represents the successive derived-functor unit maps for $q_*$ and $s_*$, followed by $Rs_*\Gamma_Q$ and these composition identifications, whereas the second path represents the single derived-functor unit for $(sp)_*$ applied to $a_!J$, after the section-preserving sheaf identification $s_*i_!q_*j_!=s_*p_*a_!$. These identifications are natural in maps of K-injective representatives and independent of the chosen resolutions $I,M,L$, as maps from the specified localized termwise source. No exactness of $q_*j_!$, $s_*i_!$ or $(sp)_*a_!$ is assumed; the units here are maps from localized termwise complexes.
